SpreadBounds

how unevenly survivors can spread
Proved in Leanring 2How survivors spread across the cycle

Any two stretches of the same length hold survivor counts differing by at most two to the number of wheels. With wheels 2 and 3 frozen, the two columns' survivor counts up to any point differ by at most two to the number of remaining wheels. Both checked numerically beforehand (4,761 cases; the column imbalance reaches 18 at the wheels up to 23, against a bound of 128).

Claims (2)

interval_spread_bound
proved in Lean
Two stretches of the same length hold survivor counts differing by at most two to the number of wheels.
/-- **The spread bound.** For prime wheels `W` and two stretches of the same
length `L`, one after position `x` and one after position `y`, the survivors
in the first exceed the survivors in the second by at most two to the number
of wheels. (Swapping the two stretches gives the bound in the other
direction.) -/
def interval_spread_bound : Prop :=
  ∀ (W : Finset Nat) (x y L : Nat), (∀ q ∈ W, q.Prime) →
    ((survivors_upto W (x + L)).card : Int) - (survivors_upto W x).card
      ≤ ((survivors_upto W (y + L)).card : Int) - (survivors_upto W y).card + 2 ^ W.card
Rests on: Sawtooth.legendre_count
Statement in Conclusions.lean ↗
Proof: RNS.SpreadBounds.interval_spread_bound_step ↗; joined to its inputs in Assemble.lean ↗
column_imbalance_bound
proved in Lean
With wheels 2 and 3 frozen, the two columns' survivor counts up to any point differ by at most two to the number of remaining wheels.
/-- **The column-imbalance bound.** For prime wheels `W` including 2 and 3 and
any bound `x`, the survivors up to `x` in the 6n-1 column and in the 6n+1
column differ by at most two to the number of wheels other than 2 and 3, in
either direction. -/
def column_imbalance_bound : Prop :=
  ∀ (W : Finset Nat) (x : Nat), (∀ q ∈ W, q.Prime) → 2 ∈ W → 3 ∈ W →
    ((column_survivors_upto W 5 x).card : Int)
        ≤ (column_survivors_upto W 1 x).card + 2 ^ (W.card - 2) ∧
      ((column_survivors_upto W 1 x).card : Int)
        ≤ (column_survivors_upto W 5 x).card + 2 ^ (W.card - 2)
Rests on: Sawtooth.column_legendre_count
Statement in Conclusions.lean ↗
Proof: RNS.SpreadBounds.column_imbalance_bound_step ↗; joined to its inputs in Assemble.lean ↗
